digest.top_line: ROAM/EORTC-1308: adjuvant IMRT 60 Gy/30 fx after GTR of WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma, DFS HR 0.51 (0.27–0.97), 5-yr DFS 79.9% vs 64.3% vs observation.
digest.tldr: The only study today is CNS: randomised adjuvant RT vs observation after complete resection of atypical meningioma, median f/u 64 mo. The ITT DFS benefit favours RT, but the trial closed short of its 46-event target. As-treated HR 0.54 (0.28–1.04) crossed 1, and recurrence was read locally in an unmasked trial.

sites.intro: Adjuvant RT vs observation after GTR of grade 2 meningioma: the trial informs the omission-vs-addition decision directly, with 8% G2-3 RT-related SAEs.

studies.name: ROAM/EORTC-1308
studies.tldr: Adjuvant IMRT 60 Gy/30 fx vs observation after complete resection of WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma: DFS HR 0.51 (0.27–0.97); 5-yr DFS 79.9% vs 64.3%.
details: 🔍 Phase 3 open-label RCT, 1:1, N=157, 58 hospitals in 11 countries
🔍 Newly diagnosed atypical meningioma, surgeon-assessed GTR (Simpson I–III), WHO PS ≤2
💊 RT arm: fractionated IMRT 60 Gy in 30 fx over 6 weeks, prospective central RTQA
🔍 CTV 5–10 mm isotropic from GTV, then 3–5 mm PTV
⚠️ Closed short of the 46-event target (41 DFS events) owing to funding constraints
⚠️ 12/78 assigned to RT never started it; 2 stopped early, biasing toward the null

subdetails: Early RT-related AEs: 30 (45%) pts, 65 G1 and 19 G2 events
Late RT-related AEs: 17 (26%), mostly hair loss, headache, fatigue
G2 or 3 RT-related SAEs: 5 (8%); no treatment-related deaths
One G2 radiation necrosis, one G2 optic neuritis with optic dose at constraint limits

details: 📊 Post-hoc molecular subset (n=132): DFS HR 0.49 (0.25–0.95); benefit held after methylation-class adjustment
⚠️ No central pathology or MRI review; recurrence read locally in an unmasked trial

verdict.rationale: First randomised evidence and primary DFS met, but accrual closed at 41 of 46 planned events, CI upper bound 0.97, and recurrence was read locally without masking.
verdict.audience: Newly diagnosed WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma after Simpson I–III resection

studies.significance: The RT effect is probably understated: 12 of 78 assigned pts never started RT, and DFS counts out-of-field and new meningiomas that a 5–10 mm CTV was never aimed at. The planned patterns-of-failure analysis will decide whether dural margins can tighten under modern IGRT, which is the next dosimetric question once adjuvant RT is adopted.
studies.monday_clinic: For a newly diagnosed WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma after surgeon-assessed Simpson I–III resection, this supports adjuvant fractionated RT over observation when recurrence prevention is the priority; it does not address subtotal resection, NF2, multiple or radiation-induced meningiomas.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **International open-label phase 3 RCT**, 1:1, 58 hospitals in 11 countries, stratified UK vs non-UK. **N=157** randomised from 990 screened; median follow-up **64 mo**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Age ≥16, **newly diagnosed atypical meningioma** after **surgeon-assessed GTR (Simpson I–III)**, WHO PS ≤2, able to start RT within 12 weeks. Excluded NF2, multiple or radiation-induced meningiomas, optic nerve sheath tumours.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **IMRT 60 Gy in 30 fx** over 6 weeks, median 2.50 mo from surgery. CTV 5–10 mm isotropic from GTV plus 3–5 mm PTV, with prospective central plan review before treatment.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** DFS, surgery to MRI-confirmed recurrence or death. Secondary: HRQoL, neurocognition (UK/Ireland), time to second-line treatment, OS, cost-effectiveness.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Early RT-related AEs in 30 (45%), all G1-2; late in 17 (26%). **G2 or 3 RT-related SAEs 5 (8%)**, including one G2 radiation necrosis and one G2 optic neuritis; no treatment-related deaths.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Before this, evidence was retrospective series and two non-randomised phase 2 cohorts reporting 3-yr PFS 88.7% (60 Gy/30 fx) and 93.8% (54 Gy/30 fx). NRG BN003 asks the same randomised question and will be the replication test.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents newly diagnosed WHO grade 2 meningioma after surgeon-assessed Simpson I–III resection. Does not represent subtotal resection, NF2, recurrent or multiple meningiomas.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: **No central pathology review** (5 pts would now be grade 3) and no mandated early postop MRI. HRQoL data fell to 38% at 5 years and neurocognition was UK/Ireland-only with ~45% missing by 24 mo, so the null QoL and cognitive findings are weak.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: With 70% of observed pts recurrence-free at 5 years, the result supports offering RT rather than mandating it. Methylation class stratifies risk but did not erase the RT effect, so it cannot yet select who to observe.

studies.interpretation:
The question this trial answers has been argued from retrospective data for two decades, and the retrospective literature never settled it because the pts who got adjuvant RT were the ones surgeons worried about. ROAM removes that selection problem, and the direction it finds is the one the non-randomised series and the two recent systematic reviews pointed to. What it adds is not a new direction but the first estimate of magnitude that is not confounded by indication: roughly a halving of the DFS hazard, with 5-year DFS 79.9% vs 64.3%.

The confidence a reader should place in that magnitude is moderate, and the reasons pull in opposite directions. Against it: the trial closed at 41 of 46 planned events, the upper CI bound sits at 0.97, and the as-treated estimate (HR 0.54, 0.28–1.04) crosses 1. Recurrence was called by unmasked local investigators without central MRI review, which matters less for a new enhancing dural nodule than for glioma but is still an unmasked subjective read in an open-label trial. For it: 12 of 78 assigned pts never started RT, which dilutes the ITT effect toward the null, and DFS is a blunt endpoint that counts out-of-field recurrence and new meningiomas elsewhere as failures of a treatment never aimed there. The authors plausibly argue the true local effect is larger. Both sets of concerns are real, and the honest summary is that the point estimate is likely right in direction and uncertain within a wide band.

OS was not different (OR 0.91, 0.27–3.05) and the trial could never have shown otherwise with 13 deaths. That makes the decision a trade between recurrence and toxicity, not survival. The toxicity side looks acceptable at 60 Gy/30 fx with central QA: late RT-related events in 26%, mostly alopecia and fatigue, but one G2 necrosis and one optic neuritis with optic dose at the constraint limit. Neurocognitive and QoL data are too incomplete to reassure or alarm.

For RT practice, the more durable questions are dosimetric. The CTV of 5–10 mm from GTV predates modern contouring consensus; the planned patterns-of-failure analysis will show whether failures were in-field, marginal along dura, or distant. If most are distant, tighter margins become defensible and the therapeutic ratio improves. The post-hoc methylation work shows the grade 2 label hides mostly methylation-class benign tumours, yet adjustment did not remove the RT effect, so biology refines prognosis without yet identifying who can safely be observed.

The result would be wrong if the local-read recurrence calls systematically favored RT, or if the truncated event count produced an early overestimate. NRG BN003 asks a closely parallel randomised question and is the obvious replication test. Until then this supports offering adjuvant RT as a default discussion after GTR, with observation a reasonable choice for older pts, easily re-resected convexity tumours, or large treatment volumes.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: IMRT 60 Gy/30 fx to a 5–10 mm CTV halved the DFS hazard (HR 0.51) with no G3+ AEs among RT-related events and one G2 necrosis. The pending patterns-of-failure analysis decides whether dural margins can tighten.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Surgeon-assessed Simpson I–III resection without early postop MRI still left 30% recurrence under observation at 64 mo. GTR alone is not definitive for atypical meningioma; authors suggest observation mainly where re-resection is easy, such as convexity tumours.

open_questions: Do patterns of failure support tighter dural margins?
Can methylation class identify pts safe to observe?
Is adjuvant RT cost-effective vs active monitoring?

related_trials.brief_title: Epigenetic Profiling and Liquid Biopsy: Perspectives for Personalized Medicine in Meningioma Patients - MIND
related_trials.brief_summary: Meningiomas are the most common primary intracranial tumors. Current treatment relies on surgical resection and radiotherapy, but molecular predictors for recurrence are lacking. This study aims to investigate epigenetic features, specifically histone post-translational modifications (PTMs) and DNA methylation, to stratify patients. The study involves a retrospective cohort to define an epigenetic signature and a prospective cohort to validate it in tissues and liquid biopsies (plasma/EVs).
